title: Online Fairness Auditing through Iterative Refinement

problem.claim: Deployed black-box machine learning models may make decisions susceptible to intrinsic bias, creating a need to audit claimed mathematical fairness guarantees.

gap.claim: Existing mechanisms require improvement for auditing probabilistic fairness assertions and monitoring fairness metrics in black-box decision systems.

contributions.claim: AVOIR reduces the number of observations required to runtime-monitor probabilistic assertions over fairness metrics defined on black-box decision functions.
AVOIR adaptively automates inference of probabilistic guarantees for estimating a wide range of fairness metrics.
AVOIR supports exploration of fairness violations aligned with governance and regulatory requirements.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Case studies on fairness metrics across three datasets report that AVOIR can detect and localize fairness violations.
The case studies report that AVOIR can help ameliorate issues caused by faulty fairness metric design.

narrative_sequence.summary: Black-box machine learning decisions can contain intrinsic biases, motivating accountability.
The work investigates mechanisms for auditing claimed mathematical fairness guarantees.
AVOIR reduces observations for runtime monitoring and adaptively infers probabilistic guarantees for fairness metrics.
The system supports exploration of fairness violations aligned with governance and regulatory requirements.
Case studies on three datasets report detection and localization of violations and mitigation of faulty metric design.

source_observation.claim: Adaptive inference can reduce the observations needed to monitor probabilistic fairness assertions.

interpretation.claim: Iterative or adaptive monitoring may make runtime fairness auditing more efficient for black-box systems.

application.claim: Use adaptive observation strategies when monitoring fairness metrics under limited runtime data.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the conditions under which observation reductions hold.

source_observation.claim: Case studies report that fairness violations can be detected, localized, and linked to faulty metric design.

interpretation.claim: Fairness auditing should examine both observed violations and the suitability of the metrics used to define them.

application.claim: Pair violation monitoring with analysis of fairness metric design in governance-oriented audits.

exception.claim: The abstract does not identify which metric designs fail or how broadly the case-study findings generalize.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the auditing algorithms or iterative refinement procedure.
The abstract does not provide quantitative results, observation reductions, or dataset names.
The abstract does not describe the probabilistic guarantees or fairness metrics in detail.
